title: Electrochemotherapy for Urinary Bladder Botryoid Rhabdomyosarcoma in a Dog: Case Report.
abstract: Urinary bladder rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is a rare malignant neoplasm in dogs, most commonly affecting young animals and frequently arising from the trigone region, where complete surgical removal is challenging. Reported median survival time for dogs with vesical RMS is 45 days, ranging from 20 to 120 days. This report describes the diagnosis and multimodal treatment of a six-month-old intact female Golden Retriever diagnosed with vesical botryoid rhabdomyosarcoma. The patient presented with urinary incontinence, dysuria, and hematuria and was initially treated for suspected cystitis without clinical improvement. Ultrasonography identified a bladder mass located in the trigone region, and exploratory cystotomy with surgical debulking was performed. Intraoperative electrochemotherapy with bleomycin was administered, followed by six sessions of systemic doxorubicin chemotherapy. Complete remission was achieved, but recurrence was noted after 183 days, and the patient presented a survival time of 277 days, exceeding previously reported outcomes for this neoplasm. Although disease progression ultimately occurred, this case suggests that incorporating electrochemotherapy into a multimodal protocol may improve locoregional control in infiltrative vesical rhabdomyosarcoma and potentially prolong survival in dogs affected by this malignancy.
